questions.prompt: Tomorrow we will praise the emperor's placid virtue with a mighty song.
questions.answer: Crās magnō carmine placidam imperātōris virtūtem laudābimus.

questions.prompt: While the enemy sleeps, you will hold the shining shield.
questions.answer: Dum hostis dormiet, splendidum scūtum tenēbis.

questions.prompt: The soldiers will fear the storm and remain in the harbor.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs tempestātem timēbunt et in portū manēbunt.

questions.prompt: Before the festival I will decorate the temple with fragrant garlands.
questions.answer: Ante fēstum templum odōrātīs sertīs decorābō.

questions.prompt: When night comes, I will lead the weary army across the river.
questions.answer: Cum nox veniet, fessum exercitum trāns flūmen dūcam.

questions.prompt: At midnight you will hear the ghost's voice in the silent house.
questions.answer: Mediā nocte phantasmatis vōcem in tacitā domō audiēs.

questions.prompt: The general will send messengers and capture the city's walls.
questions.answer: Imperātor nūntiōs mittet et urbis moenia capiet.

questions.prompt: While the poet rests in the shade, we will write many letters.
questions.answer: Dum poēta in umbrā quiēscet, multās epistulās scrībēmus.

questions.prompt: You will be a famous leader if you conquer the enemy in battle.
questions.answer: Clārus dux eris, sī hostem in proeliō vincēs.

questions.prompt: There will be great joy when the wandering exile returns home.
questions.answer: Magnum gaudium erit, cum errāns exsul domum redībit.

questions.prompt: We will be safe within the walls, but the fields will burn.
questions.answer: Intrā mūrōs tūtī erimus, sed agrī ārdēbunt.

questions.prompt: The returning soldier will carry off the spoils won in war.
questions.answer: Rediēns mīles praedam bellō partam portābit.

questions.prompt: Because the winds are favorable, we will sail to the Syrian shore.
questions.answer: Quod ventī secundī sunt, ad syriacum lītus nāvigābimus.

questions.prompt: The king, moved by pity, will free the wretched captives.
questions.answer: Rēx, misericordiā mōtus, miserābilēs captīvōs līberābit.

questions.prompt: Once the city has been captured, the victors will rule the whole land.
questions.answer: Urbe captā, victōrēs tōtam terram regent.

questions.prompt: Overcome by longing, the old man will seek his distant homeland.
questions.answer: Dēsīderiō victus, senex remōtam patriam petet.

questions.prompt: You will feel shame when the crowd praises your idle games.
questions.answer: Ruborem sentiēs, cum turba ignāvōs lūsūs tuōs laudābit.

questions.prompt: The maiden will spin wool with her distaff through the long night.
questions.answer: Virgō colō lānam per longam noctem dūcet.

questions.prompt: At dinner we will taste the Lucanian sausage and drink sweet wine.
questions.answer: In cēnā lucānicam gustābimus et dulce vīnum bibēmus.

questions.prompt: The powerful queen will adorn her hair with Syrian gems.
questions.answer: Potēns rēgīna crīnēs syriacīs gemmīs decorābit.

questions.prompt: After the shipwreck, the sailors will wander long over unknown seas.
questions.answer: Post naufragium nautae diū per ignōta maria errābunt.

questions.prompt: If the winds are favorable, the sailors will loosen the sails at first light.
questions.answer: Sī ventī secundī erunt, nautae vēla prīmā lūce solvent.

questions.prompt: The greedy lover will endure many hardships for his beloved.
questions.answer: Amātor avidus multōs labōrēs prō amātā suā sufferet.

questions.prompt: You will be a witness of this great experiment tomorrow.
questions.answer: Huius magnī experīmentī testis crās eris.

questions.prompt: The soldiers will hear the trumpet and will seize their weapons.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs tubam audient et arma capient.

questions.prompt: You will rule the vast kingdom with a firm hand.
questions.answer: Vastum rēgnum firmā manū regētis.

questions.prompt: When spring returns, the birds will rejoice in the green fields.
questions.answer: Cum vēr redībit, volucrēs in agrīs viridibus gaudēbunt.

questions.prompt: I will warn my friends about the difficult condition of peace.
questions.answer: Amīcōs meōs dē difficilī condiciōne pācis monēbō.

questions.prompt: The philosopher will teach that the soul is immortal.
questions.answer: Philosophus animam immortālem esse docēbit.

questions.prompt: We will cross the narrow strait with a light ship.
questions.answer: Angustum fretum levī nāve trānsībimus.

questions.prompt: You will find the hidden path through the dark forest.
questions.answer: Occultam viam per silvam obscūram inveniēs.

questions.prompt: The captured king will lose his kingdom and his life.
questions.answer: Rēx captus rēgnum et vītam āmittet.

questions.prompt: If you work hard, you will win a great reward.
questions.answer: Sī strēnuē labōrābis, magnum praemium capiēs.

questions.prompt: The frozen traveler will seek shelter in a poor hut.
questions.answer: Viātor algēns in casā paupere perfugium petet.

questions.prompt: We will drink cold water from the clear spring.
questions.answer: Frīgidam aquam ē fonte limpidō bibēmus.

questions.prompt: You will be safe within the city walls.
questions.answer: Intrā moenia urbis tūtī eritis.

questions.prompt: The orator will move the crowd with his eloquent speech.
questions.answer: Ōrātor turbam ōrātiōne disertā movēbit.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow the farmers will plow the wide fields before sunrise.
questions.answer: Crās agricolae lātōs agrōs ante ortum sōlis arābunt.

questions.prompt: You will send a letter to the general about the new plan.
questions.answer: Epistulam ad ducem dē novō cōnsiliō mittēs.

questions.prompt: The wise woman will nourish the sick child with gentle care.
questions.answer: Sapiēns fēmina aegrum īnfantem mollī cūrā alet.

questions.prompt: When the war ceases, the citizens will rebuild the overturned temples.
questions.answer: Ubi bellum cessābit, cīvēs templa ēversa reficient.

questions.prompt: The huntress will chase the swift stags through the mountains.
questions.answer: Vēnātrīx celerēs cervōs per montēs captābit.

questions.prompt: We will open the gates and welcome the returning victors.
questions.answer: Portās aperiēmus et victōrēs redeuntēs excipiēmus.

questions.prompt: You will not fear death if you love virtue.
questions.answer: Mortem nōn timēbitis sī virtūtem amābitis.
